speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing agitation and notice you have a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes. To help me understand what is happening, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your recent drug use and high-risk sexual behaviors, I need to know if you have experienced any fevers, chills, or pain in your right upper quadrant of your abdomen. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel; REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis C infection.

The significantly elevated bilirubin (25 mg/dL) alongside high AST/ALT levels, combined with your history of high-risk sexual behaviors, strongly suggests an acute viral hepatitis infection, specifically Hepatitis C, though acute Hepatitis B or A remain differentials pending serology. Given the severity of the jaundice and coagulopathy (INR 1.5), we must rule out acute liver failure. Do you have any specific allergies to medications, and have you been vaccinated for Hepatitis A or B in the past? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Serology_Panel; REQUEST TEST: HIV_Antibody_Antigen.
